facts.raw_span: A 68-year-old man
pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
underwent Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) in the right eye
history of an eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa (pine processionary) 9 months before DSAEK
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
no pain with ocular movements
brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, and no epithelial defect
The anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography of the right eye revealed a central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma

concepts.why: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on anterior segment optical coherence tomography suggest fungal keratitis.
The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the absence of conjunctival hyperemia, discharge, and epithelial defect suggest bacterial keratitis.

The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on anterior segment optical coherence tomography suggest Acanthamoeba keratitis.
The history of recent DSAEK surgery and the presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma suggest postoperative keratitis.

The history of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa 9 months before DSAEK and the presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma suggest Thaumetopoea pityocampa keratitis.
The history of recent DSAEK surgery and the presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma suggest corneal graft rejection.

The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on anterior segment optical coherence tomography suggest herpes simplex keratitis.

The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on anterior segment optical coherence tomography suggest varicella-zoster keratitis.

rationales.F03: The patient underwent DSAEK, which increases the risk of postoperative keratitis and corneal graft rejection.
rationales.F04: The patient has a history of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa, which could be related to the current condition.
rationales.F08: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma is a strong indicator of keratitis.
rationales.F12: The anterior segment optical coherence tomography results show a central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma, which is consistent with keratitis.
